en.headline: Lee honours Hong Kong athletes for record Asian Games medal haul
en.dek: Chief Executive John Lee presented certificates to top performers at a Monday ceremony after the team won 11 golds and 54 medals in total at the Aichi-Nagoya Games.
body: Chief Executive John Lee on Monday commended Hong Kong, China athletes for their performances at the Asian Games, where the delegation secured its best result to date.

The team won 54 medals in total, comprising 11 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze, setting new highs in both the gold count and overall tally. Lee noted during the commendation ceremony that athletes’ willingness to compete through injuries and to fight back when behind had earned deep respect.

He presented certificates to top-performing athletes, including wushu athlete Lydia Sham, who claimed the city’s first gold of the Games. Lee said the government would continue to invest in sports development, with resources reaching about HK$8.1 billion in the 2026-27 financial year, nearly 70 per cent higher than a decade earlier.
Chief Secretary Eric Chan, Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism Rosanna Law, and Sports Federation & Olympic Committee of Hong Kong, China president Timothy Fok also attended the ceremony.

zh.headline: 李家超嘉許亞運港隊創紀錄獎牌表現
zh.dek: 行政長官周一舉行嘉許禮，向名古屋亞運表現卓越的運動員頒發證書，港隊共奪11金、54面獎牌。
body: 行政長官李家超周一嘉許中國香港運動員在名古屋亞運會的表現，代表團取得歷來最佳成績。
港隊合共贏得54面獎牌，包括11金、19銀及24銅，金牌及總獎牌數目均創下新高。李家超在嘉許禮上表示，運動員即使受傷仍堅持比賽，落後時仍努力追趕，展現的拼搏精神令人敬佩。
他向表現突出的運動員頒發證書，包括奪得本屆賽事首金的武術運動員沈麗雅。李家超重申政府會繼續投放資源發展體育，2026至27財政年度體育發展開支約81億元，較十年前增加近七成。
政務司司長陳國基、文化體育及旅遊局局長羅淑佩，以及中國香港體育協會暨奧林匹克委員會會長霍震霖等亦出席儀式。
